historical_basis: In European folklore and myth the Erlking is a sinister elf lingering in the woods, stalking children who stay too long and killing them with a single touch. The name Erlking (Erlkönig, 'alder-king') was used in German Romanticism for a spirit or 'king of the fairies' and is usually thought to derive from Danish folklore's ellekonge (older elverkonge, 'elf-king'). The name was first used by Johann Gottfried Herder in Erlkönigs Tochter (1778), adapted from the Danish ballad Hr. Oluf han rider (1739), then taken up by Goethe in Erlkönig (1782), set by Schubert and others; Goethe added a new sense, 'Erl' meaning 'black alder', not 'elf'.
